To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a novel nanoscale 2 dimensional ceramic nanofiller has successfully been developed from 312 MAX phase Ti3SiC, which has shown excellent mechanical, thermal and tribological properties in an epoxy matrix.

a new type of ceramic nanostructure has been identified from the MAX phase family, which can be chemically interacted with epoxy matrix to form a self lubricating tribo film that decreases the coefficient of friction and wear rate of the composite.
the 312 MAX phase Ti3SiC 2 nanofiller is a chemically interactive functional filler that improves mechanical strength, hardness, and wear resistance of the polymer matrix.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the processing, characterization and application of a novel MAX phase CDCN nanostructure as an effective filler for obtaining high performance polymer nanocomposites for structural applications.
the development of a novel 2 dimensional ceramic nanofiller from MAX phase family, its synthesis, characterization and application as a functional filler for epoxy nanocomposites.
the development of a chemically interactive nanofiller for damage tolerant polymer composites.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, the CDCN filler offers a self lubricated interface that reduces wear and friction and also produces mechanically reliable, chemically homogeneous, damage tolerant, high modulus, high strength epoxy composites.
, CDCN nanofillers have a potential to be used as a functional nanoscale additive in polymer matrix nanocomposites for various engineering applications.
, the CDCN filler offers a unique opportunity to design high performance polymer nanocomposites with improved mechanical, tribological and thermal properties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, MAX phase CDCN nanostructure is a potential candidate for future engineering composites.
, CDCN is a promising functional nano filler for epoxy composites and it has been successfully demonstrated as a potential candidate for self lubricating, damage tolerant epoxy composites.

, the MAX phase ternary Carbide derived ceramic nanostructures (CDCN) are chemically interactive functional nanofillers which can be utilized for obtaining damage tolerant, self lubricating, high strength, high modulus, and high hardness polymer nanocomposites for advanced engineering applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, MAX phase CDCN can be processed out of bulk MAX phase carbide and can be used as a functional nanoscale filler in polymer nanocomposites.
MAX phase carbide can be used as a functional filler in polymer nanocomposites for high performance engineering applications.
, MAX phase CDCN nanofillers have potential to be used as functional nanofiller in polymer composites for high strength and damage tolerance.
